## Falcon
Front matter: client: Brightwater Bank; project: Project Falcon; people: Dana Okafor
Project Falcon moves the card payment ledger of Brightwater Bank from Oracle to PostgreSQL on Kubernetes. Dana Okafor is the product owner. Hosting must stay in the EU, PCI DSS applies, team of six.

## Notes-2026-10
Client: Marlow Retail Group
Project: Orchard
People: Lena Voss, Tomas Brandt

Orchard replaces the nightly stock export with a Kafka stream into Snowflake. dbt models build the reporting layer. GDPR applies and releases are weekly.

## A
Front matter: client: Nimbus Telecom
Nimbus Telecom runs billing on a COBOL batch system. The plan is to wrap it with REST services in Go and move reporting to BigQuery. Change windows are monthly.

## B
Front matter: client: Ostrava Steelworks
Ostrava Steelworks collects sensor data from rolling mills with MQTT into InfluxDB. Grafana dashboards are used by the shift leads. Everything stays on premises.

## Platform-Review
We run the review for Harbourline Logistics. The internal code name of the platform is Gannet. Priya Raman leads the team of eight. The stack is Java 21, Spring Boot and Oracle, deployed on OpenShift. Audit logs must be kept for ten years.

## Météo
Front matter: client: Société Générale des Eaux du Rhône (SGER)
SGER wants leak detection for its water network. Zoë Laurençon is the sponsor; Björn Åkesson builds the models. Sensor readings arrive over LoRaWAN, land in TimescaleDB and a PyTorch model flags anomalies. The SGER security team requires ISO 27001.

## Portfolio
Front matter: client: Northgate Rail
Northgate Rail runs three programmes with us. Signal: a Rust service that reads track sensors over OPC UA. Timetable: a planning tool in C# on .NET 8 with SQL Server. Fares: a ticket pricing API in Node.js on AWS Lambda. All three must meet the EN 50128 safety standard where they touch operations.
